Post-fork history of specialized copied Arbitrum gateways
Research date: 29 September 2026. This study audits recorded PulseChain transactions and public read-
only state. It neither constructs transactions nor infers participants' motives or independently verified
source-chain backing.
Findings
The selected specialized gateways produced two post-fork withdrawal events: one LPT escrow
release and the previously identified ARB issuance. The LPT transaction is an additional observed bridge
execution, not another mint. No withdrawal event was returned for HGOLD, WETH, or the retired LPT
gateway.
T ogether with the separately reconciled GRT transaction, the currently confirmed specialized destination
issuance cases remain ARB and GRT. Source code also identifies LPT and HGOLD issuance branches,
but source capability and historical execution must be reported separately.

GRT's separately confirmed shortfall mint is described in the gateway inventory (Appendix 4). Its event
and transaction were not counted again in the five-gateway search above.
Pin, coverage and method
Chain: PulseChain 369. Search interval: 17,233,000 through 27,659,393 inclusive, after the inherited
Ethereum boundary. Endpoint hash: 0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275.
The event signature is WithdrawalFinalized(address,address,address,uint256,uint256), taken from the retained
verified gateway ABIs. For each returned event the collector checked receipt inclusion, receipt success
and agreement among log, receipt, transaction and block-header hashes. It checked the pinned endpoint
again after collection. Both gateway batches completed with zero query errors. Every returned
withdrawal was examined, rather than sampling a subset.
Each observed withdrawal then received an independent transaction trace and historical totalSupply()
reads at the preceding block and transaction block. T oken zero-address Transfer searches provide a
separate cross-check for ARB, HGOLD and LPT. WETH uses its Deposit(address,uint256) event, restricted to
the selected gateway as the indexed recipient: treating every WETH deposit as a bridge mint would
conflate unrelated native-currency wrapping with bridging.
This is a census of the named gateways and signatures within the stated range. It is not a chain-wide
census of all bridges, tokens, issuance interfaces or unlogged actions. Returned history depends on the
public RPC's completeness. The retired gateway was included because inspecting only currently selected
router destinations can miss earlier integrations.
LPT: an executed escrow release
Transaction 0x377c6bd1… executed at block 21,402,997, 13 September 2024, 13:57:55 UTC, hash 
0x5488cda163f2cf7883c4aa3da3e71b79d2f0f9af61ff93910b3386e13963b9ba.
The receipt records 10,459,514.129760763228599483 LPT moving from escrow 
0x6a23f4940bd5ba117da261f98aae51a8bffa210a to 0x42543853a72edb6f1ff9bddab0cf4676187ec28a. The transaction sender
is that same recipient address. The gateway emits WithdrawalFinalized for the amount.
The retained 13-entry trace passes through the outbox and bridge into the LPT gateway. The gateway
calls the LPT token's balanceOf and transferFrom. It does not call the external minter. No zero-address
mint appears in this receipt. T otal supply is 24,918,514.377941353891894504 LPT both before and
after the block.
The verified gateway source has two branches. When escrow covers the incoming amount it transfers
existing tokens; only a shortfall invokes the external minter's bridgeMint. This observed transaction
executed the first branch. Accordingly, it does not resolve the separate question of whether the
configured minter would accept that gateway's issuance call under other circumstances.
ARB: previously identified issuance independently reconciled
Transaction 0xeebae5bc… executed at block 21,469,490, 21 September 2024, 11:15:05 UTC, hash 
0xbbcb9b58dce7934e35e967f4b96f8810c8d47625ffe6490eb4b1cffdbe195f60.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 125

The 16-entry trace includes the reverse gateway calling the exact L1 ARB token's bridgeMint. The receipt
contains a zero-address Transfer to 0x42543853a72edb6f1ff9bddab0cf4676187ec28a. Its amount and the historical
supply increase both equal 972,406,600,390,402,296,078,726,883,998.977902572465996426
ARB.
The independent token-event search, completed as eleven disjoint block ranges, returned exactly this
one post-fork zero-address Transfer. This confirms the previous destination-issuance finding. It does not
independently establish source-chain collateral or a dollar valuation for the minted quantity.
The LPT and ARB transactions share the same externally visible sender/recipient address. This is an
address-level relationship, not proof of a particular human owner or a common purpose.
Bounded negatives and recovered query failures
HGOLD returned no zero-address token Transfer and no selected gateway withdrawal for the full post-
fork interval. WETH returned no selected gateway withdrawal and no Deposit with this gateway as
recipient. The retired LPT gateway returned no selected withdrawal. These negative observations do not
establish that the contracts are incapable of execution or that no other route exists.
Some independent token-log requests returned truncated JSON, literally {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1, rather
than a valid result or structured RPC error. The original failures were retained and failed ranges were
partitioned and retried. ARB's complete interval was recovered with million-block partitions. LPT required
progressively smaller partitions, with the final 100,000-block failed interval recovered as ten successful
10,000-block queries. No unresolved range gap remains in these selected token-log searches.
The full post-fork LPT token search returned zero zero-address Transfers. This is a negative observation
for that event signature and address, not proof that every possible form of supply accounting must emit
that event. Independently, both LPT gateway-withdrawal searches completed successfully for the entire
interval, and the sole returned withdrawal was reconciled as an escrow release. Failed responses were
never treated as empty results.
Consequence for the white paper
The evidence supports a destination-accounting taxonomy grounded in actual transactions: escrow
release (LPT), direct token issuance (ARB), and authorized shortfall issuance (GRT). Native-
currency wrapping is a separate source-defined WETH behavior for which this batch found no post-fork
gateway execution.
An event named WithdrawalFinalized establishes neither new issuance nor its absence by itself.
Classification requires the token movements, executed call path and relevant supply/accounting
changes. Likewise, source containing a mint branch is insufficient evidence that the branch was used.
This distinction allows the paper to acknowledge multiple specialized issuance mechanisms without
attributing them to ordinary stablecoin routes or claiming unobserved backing.
Reproduction references
Gateway queries use the existing read-only collector: Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py, with
manifests Research/experiments/parb_specialized_mint_history_20260929.json and Research/experiments/
parb_retired_lpt_history_20260929.json. The independent token/trace/supply scope is recorded in Research/
experiments/parb_specialized_token_issuance_history_20260929.json.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 126

Raw request/response records, receipts, block headers, traces, historical supply reads and unsuccessful
responses are retained under ignored artifacts/parb-specialized-mint-history-20260929/, with a SHA-256 file
manifest. Gateway verified sources are preserved in the prior gateway-inventory batch; the retired
gateway source is in the escrow-gateway-withdrawals batch. No public state changes, transaction
simulations or signing were used in this study.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 127
